title: Predict customer churn, end to end
summary: Take a messy tabular dataset from raw CSV to a calibrated, explained model served behind an API.
brief: Pick a public churn, credit-default or loan dataset (Kaggle and the UCI repository have several). The point is not the model: it is a leak-free pipeline, an honest validation scheme, a baseline you beat, and an explanation of what drives the predictions.

milestones.text: Write the problem statement and the metric you will optimize
milestones.detail: Who acts on the prediction, and what does a false positive cost compared with a false negative?

milestones.text: Explore the data and list leakage suspects
milestones.detail: Missingness, target balance, features only known after the outcome.

milestones.text: Build a leak-free preprocessing pipeline with a logistic-regression baseline
Train and tune a gradient-boosted model with cross-validation
Choose a decision threshold from costs and report precision, recall and PR-AUC on a held-out test set
Explain the model with SHAP and check performance per customer segment
Serve the model with FastAPI in Docker and write the README

rubric: Test set touched once, at the end
Every preprocessing step lives inside the pipeline
A clear statement of which features matter and for whom the model is weaker
stretch: Add probability calibration and a reliability diagram
Simulate drift and add a PSI monitor

title: Fine-tune an image classifier and deploy it
summary: Collect your own images, fine-tune a pretrained backbone, and ship a fast, quantized model behind an API.
brief: Choose a problem you care about: local plant diseases, product categories for an online shop, or document types. Collect a few hundred images per class, keep a test set from different days or devices, and measure what fine-tuning really buys you.

milestones.text: Collect and label at least 300 images per class with a clean train/validation/test split
Train a linear probe on frozen features as the baseline
Fine-tune the backbone with augmentation and a lower learning rate
Inspect the confusion matrix and the 20 most confident mistakes
Export to ONNX, quantize to int8 and measure latency and accuracy before and after
Deploy an upload-and-predict demo and write up the results

rubric: Test images come from conditions not seen in training
Latency is measured on the target hardware
The write-up explains the failure cases
stretch: Distil into a smaller student model

title: Build a RAG assistant with evaluations
summary: A question-answering assistant over a real document collection, with hybrid search, citations and an evaluation suite that runs on every change.
brief: Use documents you have access to and that people actually ask about: university regulations, a product manual, public laws or your agency's internal docs (with permission). Quality comes from retrieval and evaluation, not from the prompt alone.

milestones.text: Write 50 realistic questions with reference answers and source passages
Ingest, clean and chunk the documents with titles and section headings
Implement BM25, dense retrieval and RRF; measure Recall@5 and MRR
Add a cross-encoder reranker and compare
Generate cited answers that can say "the sources don't say"
Score faithfulness and correctness with an LLM judge checked against your own ratings
Add injection test cases and a cost-per-query report; run the suite in CI

rubric: Retrieval and generation are evaluated separately
Every answer links to its sources
Known failure cases are listed with examples
stretch: Support Arabic and French questions with a multilingual embedder
Add query rewriting for follow-up questions in a chat

title: Make a small model beat a big one on one task
summary: Fine-tune a small open model with QLoRA so that, on one narrow task, it matches or beats prompting a much larger model at a fraction of the cost.
brief: Pick a task with clear right answers: structured extraction from invoices, classifying support tickets in Darija, or SQL generation for a fixed schema. Build the evaluation first, then the training data.

milestones.text: Define the task, output format and an automatic metric
Measure baselines: the small model prompted, and a large model prompted
Build 1,000+ training examples (labelled, or generated by a strong model and filtered)
Fine-tune with QLoRA and track validation metrics
Compare quality, latency and cost per 1,000 requests
Publish the adapter, the evaluation set and a write-up

rubric: The test set is not used to build training data
Cost and latency are reported, not only accuracy
stretch: Serve the model with vLLM and load-test it

title: Train a language model from scratch
summary: Tokenizer, data pipeline, GPT model, training loop and sampling, all written by you and trained on a single GPU.
brief: Follow the end-to-end lesson in the LLM course, then go further: train on text in a language you know, compare tokenizers, and run small scaling experiments of your own.

milestones.text: Collect and clean 100 MB or more of text
Train a byte-level BPE tokenizer and report tokens per word
Implement the GPT model and check the initial loss is about ln(vocab size)
Train with warmup, cosine decay, bf16 and gradient clipping; plot the loss curves
Run three model sizes and plot validation loss against compute
Write up samples, curves and what you learned

rubric: Loss curves for train and validation are shown
The code runs from a single command
stretch: Add RoPE and compare with learned positions
Instruction-tune it on a small chat dataset

title: Track and control a simulated robot
summary: A simulated mobile robot that estimates its position with a Kalman filter, plans with A*, and follows the path with a PID controller.
brief: Use a simple 2-D simulator you write yourself (or a library such as PyBullet or a Gymnasium environment). The aim is to connect estimation, planning and control in one loop and to measure how each part affects the result.

milestones.text: Simulate a differential-drive robot with noisy odometry and noisy position sensing
Implement a Kalman filter and plot the estimate against ground truth
Plan a path on an occupancy grid with A*
Follow the path with a PID controller and tune it
Measure tracking error with and without the filter
Record an animation and write up the results

rubric: Noise levels are stated and varied
Plots show estimate, measurement and truth together
stretch: Replace the PID with a policy trained by PPO and compare
Add a particle filter for global localization
